title: Elodie and the Colony
premise: Lena Winterbourne, a xenolinguist stranded on the dying colony of Meridian's Rest, has spent years translating the silent signals of an alien hive-organism beneath the ice — and losing her own human dreams in the process. When gravity flickers system-wide for nine seconds, she realizes the organism is not dying with the colony but broadcasting through it, and that her translations have been carrying its message all along. As the fleet's fragile truce expires, Lena must choose between delivering the organism's final transmission — proof that could end the war or ignite it — and preserving the last shreds of her human self. She delivers it, sacrificing her memories of home to become the colony's living archive, and the war ends not with victory but with both sides inheriting a shared, alien grief.
about_author: Emrys Sandoval is the pen name of a former deep-sea acoustics researcher who spent five years listening to hydrophone recordings no one else wanted to hear. They write quiet science fiction about people who talk to things that cannot answer back.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. On forgotten Meridian's Rest, Lena records the colony's slow decay and her nightly conversations with the ice-hive, noticing she now dreams in its rhythms instead of English. Then gravity stutters across the entire system for nine seconds, and every instrument on the planet points at her — as if she caused it. Emotional beat: eerie isolation sharpening into dread of being seen.

chapters.title: The Grammar of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, intercut with fleet transmissions she intercepts. Decoding the nine-second pulse, she discovers the hive embedded a message inside her own translation logs — addressed to both warring fleets, using her voiceprint. The truce expires in eleven days; a salvage crew arrives hunting whoever triggered the anomaly. Emotional beat: compulsion and guilt, realizing she was never just an observer.

chapters.title: What the Ice Remembers
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The salvage crew corners her at the relay station while the hive begins consuming her human memories to complete the message — she forgets her sister's face mid-sentence. To transmit, she must surrender everything she was. Climax: she opens the channel as the crew breaches the door, choosing inheritance over identity. Emotional beat: terrible, willing sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Language With No Word for Alone
chapters.summary: Split POV between Lena-as-archive and the fleet officers receiving the transmission. The message forces both sides to hear their dead translated into one shared voice; the war dissolves into joint mourning rather than victory. Lena remains on Meridian's Rest, no longer fully human but finally belonging — the colony's memory, dreaming in every language at once. Emotional beat: bittersweet transcendence and peace.
